description: Transforms its input with a cubic polynomial: a times x cubed, plus b times x squared, plus c times x, plus d

params.text: Sets how much of x cubed is added to the result, -2 to 2
Sets how much of x squared is added to the result, -2 to 2; it can produce a large DC offset
Sets how much of x is added to the result, -2 to 2, which makes it an attenuverter on the input
Adds a constant to the result, reaching -10 to 10V with the OUT gain at 100%; it can produce a large DC offset
Scales the input before the polynomial is applied, 0 to 200%; a 5V input at 100% gives an x of 1
Scales the result before it leaves the module, 0 to 200%

inputs.text: The signal to transform, scaled by the IN gain knob to give x
Modulates the amount of x cubed added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the amount of x squared added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the amount of x added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the constant added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the input gain; every 1V here turns the IN knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the output gain; every 1V here turns the OUT knob a tenth of its travel clockwise

outputs.text: The transformed signal, which can run far outside -5 to 5V; use the IN and OUT gain knobs to keep an audio signal in range

notes: the module is mono: it reads the first channel of a polyphonic cable and ignores the rest, and every output carries a single channel
